newsitem.title: USA: Calif. retail gasoline prices up in March - CSAA.
newsitem.headline: Calif. retail gasoline prices up in March - CSAA.

text.p: Retail gas prices in northern California and Nevada continue to rise in March, as the region's refiners run at reduced production, the California State Automobile Association (CSAA) said Monday.

Self-serve unleaded averages $1.37 a gallon in northern California, up two cents compared to CSAA's February 20, 1997, Fuel Gauge Survey. The regional average in northern California and Nevada firmed two to six cents compared to last month.

"Gasoline production has not reached full capacity in California due to the partial shutdown of several refineries for maintenance and the recent fire at the Tosco Martinez plant," said CSAA spokesman Ron Kennedy.

Hayward and Sacramento's averages rose two cents to $1.40 and $1.36. Oakland and Santa Rosa's averages are up one cent to $1.38 a gallon. Stockton and Fresno's averages rose one cent to $1.37 and $1.29, the survey reported.
However, the Santa Cruz average dropped three cents to $1.36 a gallon. Monterey's average dipped one cent to $1.37. The
national average for self-serve unleaded gasoline is $1.29, up eleven cents compared to one year ago.
In Nevada, the average for self-serve regular unleaded has risen two cents to $1.37. The Las Vegas and Reno averages rose one cent to $1.36 and $1.39.
Utah's average for self-serve regular unleaded dropped two cents to $1.23 a gallon. In Salt Lake City, the average fell two cents to $1.25.
Motorists may see pump prices at individual retailers which vary from the survey averages.
CSAA provides an array of automotive, travel, financial and insurance services to 3.7 million members in California, Nevada and Utah.
